A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, appendices, equations, figures, and tables. Retained and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original diffing, correlation-discovery, clustering, and retrieval experiments, plus OpenAI model-generation and Tulu-3 case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original results across the four analysis tasks and both case studies, and adds Gemma SAE evaluations in Appendix H.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the SAE embedding construction and all four analysis procedures. Appendix H tests alternative reader models and SAE configurations without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The Gemma experiments reuse the movie and tone datasets, injected correlations, synthetic news, and six retrieval corpora. Original dataset coverage and case-study scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain their LLM, correlated-topic-model, dense-embedding, instruction-tuned-embedding, and retrieval comparators. The added Gemma evaluations are configurations of the proposed SAE approach.

E3.justification: Appendix H substantially expands evaluation configurations beyond the existing Llama comparisons: pretrained Gemma 2B with 16k/65k SAEs across verification tasks, and five Gemma model/width combinations for retrieval, including Gemma 9B. These are additional settings; the original protocols remain.

E4.justification: New Appendix H tests whether findings transfer across reader families, model sizes, SAE widths, and pretrained versus instruction-tuned readers. It adds robustness evidence across all four tasks, including correlation-recovery failures, beyond the retained Llama reader-size and domain analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-sample surface-similarity evaluation, ten dataset shuffles, and the existing distributional summaries. The Gemma experiments introduce no newly specified repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 28–31 add substantial Gemma results: movie/tone similarity means of 0.40/0.31 for 16k and 0.47/0.39 for 65k, failure of the 16k SAE to recover injected correlations, clustering matrices, and retrieval comparisons. These are newly evaluated configurations; original benchmark and case-study results are retained.

T1.justification: The SAE equations, correlation definitions, retrieval metrics, and normalized-average-precision construction are retained. No new or revised formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the four-task contribution, cost and reliability claims, controllability claims, and two model-behavior case studies. The rewritten conclusion preserves the same central argument for data-centric interpretability.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds substantive qualifications: label diversity may explain better diffing with wider SAEs, missing relevant latents may explain the 16k correlation failures, and SAE width appears more influential than reader size for retrieval. Existing interpretations and limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix H identifies GemmaScope SAEs, Neuronpedia labels, and the model/width configurations used. Conversely, v2 removes the project-code link printed on v1's first page. Most existing prompts and implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to GemmaScope and Neuronpedia for the new experiments. Existing cited works and the central research positioning are retained; Section 2 also explicitly includes topic models among traditional interpretable representations.

P1.justification: There are localized prose revisions, a shorter conclusion, an appendix contents page, revised acknowledgements, and a generic impact statement. The LLM usage appendix is removed and some appendix organization changes, while the main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference main text, with substantial figure rearrangement and table relocation. Figures 3–5 and 8 are reformatted, and four Gemma figures are added. Existing content such as the latent-predictability table is relocated rather than removed.

improvement.justification: Appendix H improves the empirical assessment by testing another reader family and revealing meaningful capacity-dependent failures, qualifying the earlier Llama-based evidence. The original findings remain intact. This useful extension outweighs the limited reproducibility drawback of removing the project-code link, but does not fundamentally transform the paper's quality.
